scoring_criteria.rationale: Most common local inference workload. Lower $/tok = better value.
Growing workload as models get larger. Only datacenter GPUs can fit 70B FP16.
Determines maximum model size and batch size. Critical for 70B+ models.
Primary bottleneck for LLM inference (memory-bound workload).
Can it be deployed standalone (PCIe card) vs requiring special infrastructure (SXM baseboard, rack)?
CUDA dominance, vLLM/TRT-LLM support, quantization tooling. AMD ROCm improving but still behind.
Can it serve multiple concurrent users? Depends on memory + NVLink scaling.
700W SXM GPUs require datacenter cooling. Consumer GPUs work anywhere.

scoring_methodology: Each GPU scored 0-100 per criterion, then weighted sum. 7B $/tok and 70B $/tok normalized against best/worst in set. Form factor: standalone PCIe card = 100, SXM with baseboard = 60, rack-only = 20. Ecosystem: CUDA = 100, ROCm = 60, Apple = 70, ASIC/hosted = 30.

weaknesses: Outperformed by RTX 5090 in every metric

strengths: 192GB HBM3 — largest of any GPU, fits 70B FP16 easily
weaknesses: vLLM support improving but not CUDA parity
80GB tight for 70B FP16 with large batches
Outperformed by H200 and MI300X in key metrics
Limited software ecosystem for LLM inference
Stage 02 peak claims (1,800-3,000 tok/s) inflated vs official 750
Sold as complete systems — can't compare per-GPU

best_overall.rationale: Best overall for local/single-GPU 7B inference. Unbeatable $/tok (0.34), consumer form factor, full CUDA ecosystem. The dominant choice for personal/local LLM deployment at 7B-13B model sizes. Caveat: can't run 70B models.

best_for_7b.rationale: Clear winner for 7B workloads. 32GB GDDR7, 5,841 tok/s, $0.34/tok. No other GPU comes close on cost efficiency for this workload.

best_for_70b.rationale: Best 70B value: 192GB HBM3 fits 70B FP16 on a single card, $15K for 2 GPUs. Per-GPU $/tok_70b ~$53-107. The ecosystem gap (ROCm vs CUDA) is the main risk, but for inference-only workloads, vLLM+ROCm support is adequate.

best_datacenter.rationale: Best datacenter GPU for 70B: 141GB HBM3e, 317 tok/s single unit, NVLink scaling to 30,000+ tok/s aggregate. Expensive ($35K) but justified for production workloads requiring high throughput and multi-stream capacity.

best_edge.rationale: Best edge option for 70B: 128GB unified memory fits 70B Q4. Low power, desktop form factor. Caveat: low confidence on throughput estimates, limited multi-stream, and narrow software ecosystem.

best_value_consumer.rationale: At $1,999 MSRP, $0.34/tok for 7B is unbeatable. Even at retail $5,000, still #1. The RTX 4090 is a distant second ($1.33/tok).

best_value_datacenter.rationale: $15K for 2x 192GB GPUs with 70B FP16 support. Per-GPU cost ~$7,500, half the price of H200. ROCm ecosystem is the risk factor.

7B-13B.rationale: Consumer GPUs dominate 7B $/tok. RTX 5090 at $0.34/tok is 27x better value than H200.

single_gpu.rationale: Only datacenter GPUs with >80GB can fit 70B FP16 comfortably. MI300X best value, H200 best performance.

multi_gpu.rationale: NVLink scaling to 30,000+ tok/s aggregate. CUDA ecosystem maturity for multi-GPU orchestration.

405B.recommendation: Multi-GPU H200 cluster or cloud API
405B.rationale: 405B FP16 requires ~800GB — needs 8x H200 or 8x MI300X minimum. Consider cloud API for infrequent use.

remaining_uncertainties: RTX 5090 throughput numbers from computeprices.com — single source, low confidence for absolute ranking
AMD MI300X per-GPU pricing uncertain — sold as 2-GPU card, per-GPU $/tok is estimated
ROCm ecosystem maturity for production inference — adequate for development but unknown for sustained high-load production
Apple M4 Max LLM throughput estimates from single source — need independent verification
RTX 5090 retail price volatility — $4,700-$7,000 range makes $/tok highly variable
Multi-GPU NVLink scaling factors not quantified — H200 aggregate throughput claims need verification
Emerging architectures (Groq, Cerebras) lack pricing transparency — hosted-only models hard to compare
SambaNova SN3000 is an 8-chip rack — per-chip performance and pricing are opaque
summary: The optimal hardware depends entirely on model size: RTX 5090 for 7B (unbeatable $/tok), AMD MI300X for 70B single-GPU (best value), NVIDIA H200 for 70B multi-GPU (best performance). There is no single winner across all model sizes. Consumer GPUs dominate small-model inference; datacenter GPUs are required for 70B+. The CUDA ecosystem advantage is real but narrowing for inference-only workloads.
